ttest_decision: The platform has already split the experiment into `group_a` and `group_b` (metric: {metric}). Compare the two groups with a Welch two-sample t-test (you may use `welch_ttest(group_a, group_b)`). Using α={alpha}, set `different` to True if the means differ significantly, otherwise False. Also store the two-sided p-value in `p_value`.
bayes: Bayes' law practice ({title}). Let A be '{event}' and B be '{evidence}'. You are given P(A)={prior}, P(B|A)={sensitivity}, and P(B|not A)={false_positive}. Using Bayes' law, P(A|B) = P(B|A) P(A) / P(B), where P(B) = P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|not A)P(not A). Compute the posterior P(A|B) and assign it to `answer` (float between 0 and 1).
ttest_relevance: Conditional A/B follow-up on `{metric}`. `group_a` and `group_b` are already split. Run a Welch t-test (you may use `welch_ttest`). The result should be close — expect a two-sided p-value somewhere between about 0.11 and 0.40. Set `different` using α={alpha}. Separately, set `relevant` to True only if you would act on this difference in a product decision (consider both statistical significance and whether the mean gap looks practically meaningful). Also store `p_value`.
